newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on overseas trend.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on overseas trend.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar recovered from its morning losses on Friday, ending higher against its U.S. counterpart on continued decline of the greenback overseas, dealers said.
The local unit closed at T$27.735 against Thursday's T$27.787, off an opening low of T$27.815.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$266.5 million.

"Persistent fund outflows in the morning had pressured the local unit, but in the afternoon demand for the greenback had sharply reduced due to continued dollar decline overseas," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"At one time, there was no demand at all for the greenback," he said.
Dealers said fund outflows in the morning were triggered by a politically-induced stock market tumble on Thursday.

The island's stock market fell by 2.27 percent on Thursday on hectic selling sparked by recent political instability amid public discontent over the government's failure to check a spate of violent crimes.
They said the Taiwan dollar rate would hover at current levels in the near term.
A T$27.70-27.78 range was seen for next week.
